address: `Reports/open-bugs-handoff.md` §S, the riser-seeded climb collapse; measured 2026-08-26
retest: Never as a box. No box can have a correct boundary here, because "correct" is not locally observable — that is the whole content of §S. A box would have to *contain a real anchor* rather than trust one, and at ~2,400 weighted steps to bedrock that means spanning the massif. **The cause turned out not to be the framework at all** — `particle::landed_cell` carries a landed particle's `aux` only for `worth_in_aux` (food) materials, so every thrown rock lands at `aux 0`, which reads as bedrock-adjacent and acts as a load sink. address: `src/sim/rng.rs` `stream` doc (the "both research reports name the wrong culprit" note); `src/sim/plant.rs` `seed_genotype` doc
retest: The residual confound is real but **binds founders only**, because `seed_genotype` returns early on `inherited` — a lineage's genetics flow parent to child and position never re-enters (`plant-evolution-design.md` §1c). What reopens it is a *measurement*, not an argument: the founder-versus-descendant fraction over a long run. If founders are a large share of a radiation run's population, a favourable cell re-sown repeatedly draws the same founding genotype and can read as "this allele wins here". address: `src/sim/decay.rs` `tick`, the "Left dry, deliberately" comment (first paragraph)
retest: Rejected as a **copy**, not as an idea. A true transfer that debits the donor by exactly what the new cell gains is conserved and is *not* covered by this rejection; any version that leaves the donor whole is the same dead end whatever cell it reads from. The rejection also leans on capillary flow being able to reach the new cell, so if `SOIL_FIELD_CAPACITY` (620) or `SOIL_CAPILLARY_REST` (380) ever move far enough that a dry cell beside damp ground no longer fills, the fallback is gone and the question reopens.

address: src/sim/plant.rs `MEAN_NIGHT_INCOME_FACTOR` (same report, §5)
`src/sim/plant.rs` fn allocate_to_frontier, the donor sort; measured 2026-08-24
retest: The bit-identity half is permanent while the sort's tie order is left to the standard library — **the lookup win and bit-identity are mutually exclusive here**, because the key can only be cached by putting it in the element. It reopens the moment an explicit positional tie-break is added to the comparator (`.then(a.cmp(b))`), which makes the order a function of the comparator alone and therefore independent of both the element type and the library's implementation. That is a behaviour change in its own right and is an owner decision, not a free one — but note the standing risk it would remove: **as written, a Rust upgrade that retunes ipnsort can silently change how every plant in the world grows**, and nothing in the suite would catch it.

address: `src/sim/plant.rs` `Behavior::Ripen` arm, the "charged from the reproductive budget" note; measured 2026-08-29
retest: The rejection depends entirely on organs being *donors* in `allocate_to_frontier`. A fruit is a strong sink in real plants, and if that function ever learns to fund organs -- the source-sink model `plant-equilibrium-costs-2026-08-27.md` §10b gestures at -- then charging at the cell becomes payable and this reopens. Note the distinction that makes the split principled rather than a workaround, and which survives either way: **construction** (building the cells) is charged at the decision from the acting cell, per the owner's 2026-08-27 ruling; **provisioning** a fruit is reproduction and belongs on the reproductive account regardless.

address: `examples/selection_arena.rs` `moisture=` / `assets/species/*.ron` `Germinate.soil_water_threshold`; measured 2026-08-30
retest: The rejection is of *soil moisture as the lever*, not of water as a selective pressure. It reopens the moment either constant moves -- lower `soil_water_threshold`, or raise the uptake price (`Absorb.rate`, `SOIL_UPTAKE_PER_TICK`) -- since those are what close the band between "a seed will start" and "water limits growth". It does **not** reopen by running the same bed longer or on more seeds. And note the deeper reason the arm was flat even in the real drought: uptake is `rate x available` per *wet neighbour*, so what earns is contact with wet soil, and in a drawn-down bed the bed sets that -- the handicap removed 23% of root cells and **3%** of uptake surface. Any change that makes contact scale with branching (a per-cell depletion zone) invalidates that half.

The positional draw was built (`PIXEL_PHYSICS_RNG=positional`, `rng::sweep`) and **the premise this entry rests on is false**: with the RNG removed from the question entirely, the two sweep arms still diverge, identical through frame 4,329 and **first differing at frame 4,330** on the standard lab bed, bisected to the frame with every arm's hash reproducing exactly across three reps. So the spans are not behaviour-neutral and never were -- the stream shift was one reason among at least two, and removing it moved the divergence from frame ~1 to frame 4,330 rather than removing it. Separately the economics collapsed: the positional draw costs **+0.149 ms/tick** at box density, which is the whole of what the spans save, so the full change end to end is 2.631 -> 2.636 ms with **overlapping ranges and no measurable gain**. The 3.0x/7.8x ceiling came from `labperf`'s `est_` columns, which are ~90% soil moisture and since #212 do not wake the sweep at all, so they fail that instrument's own stated control. **Do not re-attempt either the spans or the positional draw as a performance change on this evidence.** What would reopen the *spans* is finding and fixing whatever makes frame 4,330 differ -- the leading unmeasured hypothesis is chunk wakefulness feeding `field::step`'s `active_chunk_count()` gate -- after which they would still have to pay for themselves without the positional draw, since it is what made them cost more than they save. Full account: Reports/sweep-positional-rng-2026-09-05.md §9.

address: `assets/species/ant.ron` / `ancestor.ron` `(Crowding, Dig, 0.6)` — density-dependent digging, the "rooms" mechanism; built, rate-matched, swept and withdrawn 2026-09-02
retest: Four conditions. **(0) The driving input's *population* actually reaches the regime the model is about, which is the one that most likely invalidates the whole run.** `Crowding` is `(crowd / crowd_scale).min(1.0)` -- **clamped at 1.0** -- and Toffin's transition is about average density along the perimeter falling *below* a critical value. Measured over 52 ants at frames 100/500/2,000/4,000, the distribution is **p90 and max pinned at 1.000 throughout, and the median 1.000, 1.000, 0.875, 0.625**: the colony never leaves the top of the range, so the low-density regime the mechanism needs is one this bed may never enter. **Note what this is not**: `min` is 0.000 and `p10` is 0.25 at every stop, so *individual* ants do read low density -- a digger alone in a gallery -- and it is the population statistic that stays saturated, which is the one Toffin's model is about. The pre-check that shipped with the first attempt asked *"is `Crowding` a dead channel?"*, and it passed; that is the question **does it vary at all**, not **does it reach the regime the mechanism requires**, and the two look identical when only the mean and the max are printed. `burrow_probe` prints min/p10/p50/mean/p90/max for exactly this reason. The general form, and it is not about ants: **an input that never leaves saturation cannot demonstrate a mechanism about its low end**, so the realised range of a driving input is a precondition of a run rather than a readout of it. (Not hard-asserted in `burrow_probe`, deliberately: it would refuse on the only bed there is, and the arm has other users -- the lining and spoil ablations -- that do not care about crowding at all.) **(1)** A bed where a colony is not dominated by quarrying the open face of a bank -- Toffin's own setup has no open face at all — in `burrow_probe`'s bed the largest void component is the eroded face and the roofed cavity is a fifth of it, so the perimeter density Toffin's model is about is not the quantity the ants are actually responding to. **(2)** Some source of positive feedback into a dug spot (`Persist` momentum, a trail into a bud), which is what the branching half needs and which is absent here — density dependence alone provably does not supply it. **(3)** A bed where ants do not starve at ~frame 4,000, since the last half of every run is a frozen final state -- and long enough for the cavity to *outgrow* the colony, which at **54 cells against 52 ants** it plainly has not. Conditions (0) and (3) are one cause seen from two ends: density never falls because the nest never gets big enough relative to the colony. The re-test is therefore a **different experiment rather than a re-run**.
